content: coffee A controlled explosion on a film set near the O2 arena in London ignited a fire that destroyed a van and damaged a car and lorry, prompting firefighters to respond to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before 8 p.m. on Saturday. The blaze was brought under control after about an hour with the help of twenty‑five firefighters, and no injuries were reported. Authorities said the fire followed a pre‑planned filming activity at the site, which is close to the venue that will host concerts by Niall Horan and Texas next week. The London Fire Brigade posted on X that the fire in Silvertown is now under control, noting that one vehicle was destroyed and most of a car and lorry suffered damage, with no injury reports. They added that the blaze stemmed from a controlled explosion on the film set that spread beyond expectation, and crews remained on the scene for the rest of the evening. The yard is also situated near London’s cable‑car link over the River Thames, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman said they are aware of reports of explosions heard in the area around the O2 in Greenwich.
